name: Mahia Peninsula, New Zealand
summary: Open pasture on the southern tip of the Mahia Peninsula, between sea cliffs on both sides. The simulation's pad centre is placed in a large grazed paddock, read from the 2023 aerial photograph and chosen on the lidar DEM as one of the flattest open spots near the tip (within 0.25 m over 10 m). The ground rolls gently beyond that, so the flat-ground assumption of the simulation is only approximate here; the relief figures give the departure.
site_note: The pack covers an existing launch site about 1.5 km south of the pad origin. The simulated vehicle, pad and mission are generic: they are not that site, its facilities, its operations or its operator, and imply no affiliation.

origin.note: The simulation's pad centre (model origin, z = 0) is placed on the detail terrain at this point; the orthometric height is that ellipsoidal height minus the EGM2008 undulation. The geoid undulation is treated as constant over the extent (its spread across the corners is given).

frame.note: Model x, y, z map to east, north, up of the tangent plane at the origin. Terrain heights are ENU up, so they include the curvature of the Earth.

height.order: row-major, row 0 at the north edge, column 0 at the west edge

registration.method: Fraction of texels where the DEM says land (> 1 m) and the image is not dark water, at zero shift and at the best shift on a 30 m lattice within 300 m.

image.processing: Bilinear resampling of the TCI asset onto the ENU grid, JPEG quality 88. No colour editing.

height.order: row-major, row 0 at the north edge, column 0 at the west edge

image.processing: Area-averaged to the texel size from the source, bilinear resampling onto the ENU grid, per-channel tone curves (colour_fit: 33 percentiles of the detail and of the base image on 10 m blocks, linearly interpolated) matching the detail image to the base image, texels without source data filled from the base image, JPEG quality 86.

layers.note: Within 192 m of the edge of this layer the drawn heights blend linearly into the base grid and the image fades into the base image, so the two surfaces meet. That margin is a display adjustment of the context data.

accuracy: Copernicus GLO-30 is a surface model: heights include buildings and vegetation canopy. Its stated absolute vertical accuracy is better than 4 m (90 % linear error); it does not resolve pads, roads or ground conditions.
The 10 m image does not resolve structures; it is context only.

The simulation assumes flat ground at z = 0 and computes no interaction with this terrain. Where the terrain rises above z = 0 the drawn trajectory may pass through it; this is a property of the geographic placement, not of the simulated flight.
Horizontal registration of image and terrain follows the sources' georeferencing; Sentinel-2 L2A geolocation is of the order of 10 m.

Detail layer (2.048 km square around the origin): heights from Hawke's Bay LiDAR 1m DEM (2020-2021), bare earth, heights in NZVD2016 (EPSG:7839, as stated in the LINZ elevation TIFF specification; not recorded in the GeoTIFF), sampled every 4 m and converted from EPSG:2193+7839 to EPSG:4959 ellipsoidal heights with PROJ (Inverse of New Zealand Transverse Mercator 2000 + Inverse of NZGD2000 to NZVD2016 height (2) (with axis order normalized for visualization)); those are used as WGS84 heights. The origin is on this surface.
LINZ states a vertical accuracy of about 20 cm for the source lidar; the tiles are LERC-compressed with a 1 mm error.
Detail image: Hawke's Bay 0.25m Rural Aerial Photos (2023-2025), red, green and blue bands of the RGBNIR cloud-optimised tiles at 0.5 m per texel (source 0.25 m), resampled onto the ENU grid.

The LINZ imagery and DEM are on NZGD2000, a semi-dynamic datum fixed at epoch 2000; read here as WGS84, they are offset from the base layers by of the order of 1 to 2 m on the ground. The images were flown on 2023-02-20 and later; the lidar is of November 2020 to January 2021.

Within 192 m of the edge of the detail layer the drawn heights blend into the base grid and the detail image fades into the base image; this display adjustment is the only change made to the context data.

check_note: Geodetic points of grid nodes and their ENU coordinates computed with pyproj; the Rust georeference crate must reproduce them within 1 mm.

features.accuracy: OSM footprints as mapped by contributors (typically 1 to 3 m). Lidar heights are the 90th percentile of first-surface heights above the lidar ground inside the footprint, from 1 m cells; the lidar date may differ from the image and OSM dates. Walls, roof shapes and materials are illustrative; roof colours are sampled from the pack image.
